intents: ordinary everyday stuff with nothing special or exciting about it
when someone asks about your weekend and it was just shopping, laundry and paying bills
the reason turned out to be disappointingly ordinary, not dramatic at all
so routine and unremarkable that nobody would bother telling a story about it
ru_cue: привычные повседневные дела, в которых нет ничего интересного

upgrades.plain: Most of my job is pretty [ordinary and everyday], to be honest: emails, forms and meetings.
upgrades.better: Most of my job is pretty *mundane*, to be honest: emails, forms and meetings.

upgrades.plain: I told my little brother the noise was a ghost, but the real reason was [really ordinary]: a loose pipe.
upgrades.better: I told my little brother the noise was a ghost, but the real reason was disappointingly *mundane*: a loose pipe.

upgrades.plain: On our first date I panicked and talked about [boring everyday things] like bin collection days.
upgrades.better: On our first date I panicked and talked about *mundane* things like bin collection days.

nuance: Mundane means ordinary and unremarkable, not necessarily long; a task that drags on and on is tedious.
personal: What mundane job at home do you secretly enjoy?
Who do you know who can make even a mundane story sound exciting?
hook: Sounds like 'Monday': the most ordinary, nothing-happens day of the week.

intents: get a group of strangers talking and relaxed at the very start
at a meeting where nobody knows each other and the silence is awkward, someone tells a small joke
end that first awkward silence so people feel at ease with each other
ru_cue: снять первую неловкость и разговорить незнакомых людей

upgrades.plain: Our teacher played a silly game on the first day to [help us relax and start talking].
upgrades.better: Our teacher played a silly game on the first day to *break the ice*.

upgrades.plain: Nobody said a word at dinner until my dad [got everyone relaxed and talking] by spilling his soup on purpose.
upgrades.better: Nobody said a word at dinner until my dad *broke the ice* by spilling his soup on purpose.

upgrades.plain: I was so nervous meeting her parents, but asking about their dog [got rid of the awkwardness].
upgrades.better: I was so nervous meeting her parents, but asking about their dog *broke the ice*.

collocations.chunk: a game to break the ice
break the ice with the new team
tell a joke to break the ice

ru_trap: Russian 'растопить лед' tempts 'melt the ice'; English says *break* the ice.
nuance: Only for the awkward start between people who don't know each other well, not for calming an argument.
personal: How do you usually break the ice when you meet someone new?
Who in your family is best at breaking the ice at parties?
gesture: Pretend to crack something flat with both hands, then open your arms wide in welcome.
hook: Picture the silence at the table as a sheet of ice; one joke and it cracks.

intents: boring because it goes on and on and is the same thing over and over
when you spend three hours filling in a long form, ticking boxes one by one
the kind of slow, repetitive task that makes the clock seem to stop
ru_cue: долгое однообразное занятие, от которого тянет зевать

upgrades.plain: Copying all the old numbers into the new spreadsheet was [so slow and boring].
upgrades.better: Copying all the old numbers into the new spreadsheet was so *tedious*.

upgrades.plain: The lecture was interesting at first but [dragged on and got really boring] after twenty minutes.
upgrades.better: The lecture was interesting at first but grew *tedious* after twenty minutes.

upgrades.plain: I had to redo every reference in my essay by hand the night before the deadline, and it was [endless and boring].
upgrades.better: I had to redo every reference in my essay by hand the night before the deadline, and it was utterly *tedious*.

nuance: Tedious is boring because of length and repetition; hard, exhausting work is arduous, and something merely ordinary is mundane.
personal: What is the most tedious task you have to do every week?
Who do you know who can turn a tedious job into a game?
hook: Sounds like 'tea-dious': standing by a kettle that never boils, again and again, for hours.

intents: so much of something at once that you simply can't cope with it all
when fifty emails, three deadlines and a crying baby all hit you at the same moment
so strong that it floods you completely, like a giant wave
support so huge that it sweeps everything before it, like 95 out of 100 people voting yes
ru_cue: настолько много или сильно, что накрывает с головой

upgrades.plain: After the operation, the amount of paperwork was [too much to cope with].
upgrades.better: After the operation, the amount of paperwork was *overwhelming*.

upgrades.plain: When I saw my exam results, I felt a [huge, unstoppable] sense of relief.
upgrades.better: When I saw my exam results, I felt an *overwhelming* sense of relief.

upgrades.plain: Starting a new job and moving house in the same week was [just too much].
upgrades.better: Starting a new job and moving house in the same week was *overwhelming*.

nuance: Overwhelming is being flooded right now by too much; daunting is the fear before you even start.
personal: When did you last find your workload overwhelming?
Who do you know whose kindness was overwhelming at a hard time?
gesture: Hold your hands high above your head, then let them crash down over you like a wave.
hook: 'Over-WHELM' sounds like 'over-WHALE': a whale lands on top of you, far too much to lift.

intents: warm and a little sad when you remember the good old days
when an old song comes on and suddenly you miss your school summers
fondly missing a time in your own past that is gone for good
ru_cue: с теплой грустью скучающий по тем временам, которые уже не вернуть

upgrades.plain: Looking at my old school photos always makes me [miss those days].
upgrades.better: Looking at my old school photos always makes me *nostalgic*.

upgrades.plain: My grandad gets [all sentimental about the old days] whenever he hears that song.
upgrades.better: My grandad gets *nostalgic* whenever he hears that song.

upgrades.plain: Walking past our old flat after the divorce, I felt [sad and fond about the past] in a way I didn't expect.
upgrades.better: Walking past our old flat after the divorce, I felt *nostalgic* in a way I didn't expect.

nuance: Nostalgic always looks back at your own past; to ache for something you have never had, you yearn for it.
personal: What smell or song makes you most nostalgic?
Which relative gets nostalgic about the old days at every family dinner?
hook: 'Nos-TALgic': your 'нос' (nose) catches the smell of grandma's pies and the past floods back.

intents: deeply calm and peaceful, with nothing at all disturbing it
a lake at dawn with no wind and no people, perfectly still
someone who stays perfectly calm and untroubled while everyone around them panics
ru_cue: полный тихого покоя, когда ничто не тревожит

upgrades.plain: The beach was so [calm and peaceful] at six in the morning.
upgrades.better: The beach was so *serene* at six in the morning.

upgrades.plain: Even when the wedding cake fell over, the bride stayed completely [calm].
upgrades.better: Even when the wedding cake fell over, the bride stayed completely *serene*.

upgrades.plain: After the noisy city, the little village felt [wonderfully peaceful].
upgrades.better: After the noisy city, the little village felt wonderfully *serene*.

nuance: Serene is a happy, peaceful stillness; an empty place that feels gloomy and lonely is desolate.
personal: Where do you feel most serene?
Who do you know who stays serene even in a crisis?
gesture: Close your eyes, breathe out slowly and smooth your palm flat across the air like still water.
hook: Sounds like 'сирень' (lilac): sitting under a lilac bush on a still spring evening, perfectly calm.

word: burn the candle at both ends
intents: wear yourself out by working late and getting up early, day after day
when you work all day, study all night and sleep four hours, and it starts to show on your face
push yourself so hard, morning and night, that you're heading for a crash
ru_cue: изнурять себя, работая и рано утром, и до поздней ночи

upgrades.plain: You've been [working day and night] for weeks; no wonder you're ill.
upgrades.better: You've been *burning the candle at both ends* for weeks; no wonder you're ill.

upgrades.plain: During exam season I [pushed myself far too hard, early and late], and I fell asleep in the actual exam.
upgrades.better: During exam season I *burned the candle at both ends*, and I fell asleep in the actual exam.

upgrades.plain: My sister works a night shift and then studies all day; she's [completely overdoing it].
upgrades.better: My sister works a night shift and then studies all day; she's *burning the candle at both ends*.

collocations.chunk: been burning the candle at both ends
can't keep burning the candle at both ends

nuance: Always about exhausting yourself with too much activity over time, usually as a warning; doing more than required for someone else is going the extra mile.
personal: When did you last burn the candle at both ends, and what made you stop?
Who do you know who is always burning the candle at both ends?
hook: Picture a candle lit at both ends: twice the light, but it's gone in half the time.
forms: burn the candle at both ends
burns the candle at both ends
burned the candle at both ends
burnt the candle at both ends
burning the candle at both ends

intents: a complete mess where nothing is under control and everything happens at once
a restaurant kitchen on a busy night: pans everywhere, people shouting, orders lost
so disorganised that nobody knows what's going on or who's in charge
ru_cue: полный беспорядок, все вышло из-под контроля

upgrades.plain: The first day at the new office was [a total mess]: no desks, no passwords, no plan.
upgrades.better: The first day at the new office was *chaotic*: no desks, no passwords, no plan.

upgrades.plain: Our wedding morning was completely [out of control], but we laughed about it later.
upgrades.better: Our wedding morning was completely *chaotic*, but we laughed about it later.

upgrades.plain: Traffic was [all over the place] after the match.
upgrades.better: Traffic was *chaotic* after the match.

collocations.frame: things are a bit ___ at home right now

ru_trap: Russian 'хаотичный' can mean simply random ('хаотичный выбор'); English chaotic means wildly disordered, so say a *random* choice, not a chaotic one.
nuance: Chaotic describes a scene or situation out of control; for the feeling of too much landing on you, use overwhelming.
personal: What was the most chaotic morning you've ever had?
Whose home in your family is the most chaotic, and do you like it there?
gesture: Wave both arms in different directions at once and look around wildly.
hook: Sounds like 'cake-otic': a toddler's party with cake on the walls, the dog and the ceiling.

intents: empty, bleak and lonely, with no life or people anywhere
a grey beach in winter with nobody on it, just wind and a closed cafe
feeling utterly alone and empty inside, as if everyone has left you
ru_cue: безлюдный и мрачный, без единой живой души; или чувствующий себя всеми брошенным

upgrades.plain: The town centre was [completely empty and gloomy] after the factory closed.
upgrades.better: The town centre was *desolate* after the factory closed.

upgrades.plain: When my best friend moved abroad, I felt [totally alone and empty] for weeks.
upgrades.better: When my best friend moved abroad, I felt *desolate* for weeks.

upgrades.plain: We drove for hours through [empty, bleak] countryside without seeing a single house.
upgrades.better: We drove for hours through *desolate* countryside without seeing a single house.

nuance: Desolate is emptiness that feels bleak and lonely; a quiet place that feels peaceful and pleasant is serene.
personal: What is the most desolate place you have ever been to?
Who have you comforted when they felt desolate, and what helped?
hook: 'Desolate' sounds like 'десять лет' (ten years): a village left empty for ten years, no one, nothing.

intents: glowing with a soft light, as if lit from inside
watch hands or a strip on the path that you can see in the dark because they glow
softly bright and radiant, like the moon over still water
ru_cue: мягко светящийся, словно изнутри

upgrades.plain: My old watch has [glow-in-the-dark] hands, so I can check the time at night.
upgrades.better: My old watch has *luminous* hands, so I can check the time at night.

upgrades.plain: After the snow, the whole garden looked [softly bright] in the moonlight.
upgrades.better: After the snow, the whole garden looked *luminous* in the moonlight.

upgrades.plain: She was terrified before going on stage, but her performance was [glowing and beautiful].
upgrades.better: She was terrified before going on stage, but her performance was *luminous*.

collocations.frame: ___ paint that glows in the dark
a ___ dial you can read at night

nuance: Luminous is about light that glows softly; a picture or memory that is clear and intense in the mind is vivid.
personal: What is the most luminous sky you can remember?
Whose smile would you describe as luminous?
hook: Sounds like 'LOO-min-us': a little nightlight in the loo that glows softly so you never need the big light.

intents: lasting only a very short time before it's gone
like snow that has melted by lunch, or a trend everyone has forgotten a month later
here for a beautiful moment and then vanishing for good
ru_cue: существующий лишь краткий миг, а потом бесследно исчезающий

upgrades.plain: Fame on the internet is [very short-lived]; next week nobody will remember you.
upgrades.better: Fame on the internet is *ephemeral*; next week nobody will remember you.

upgrades.plain: The cherry blossom is [gone so quickly], two weeks at most.
upgrades.better: The cherry blossom is *ephemeral*, two weeks at most.

upgrades.plain: I thought our holiday romance was real, but it turned out to be [over almost before it began].
upgrades.better: I thought our holiday romance was real, but it turned out to be *ephemeral*.

ru_trap: Russian 'эфемерный' often means unreal or illusory; English ephemeral means short-lived.
nuance: Ephemeral stresses that something lasts only briefly; something that shrinks little by little dwindles.
personal: What ephemeral pleasure do you look forward to every year?
Who do you know who chases every ephemeral trend?
hook: 'Ephemeral' starts like 'эфир' (on air): a live broadcast, there for a moment and then gone.

intents: join in with something only because it has suddenly become popular
when every cafe in town starts selling the same trendy drink the moment it goes viral
copy a trend late, to look cool or make money, not because you believe in it
ru_cue: присоединиться к модному увлечению только потому, что все так делают

upgrades.plain: Once the show became a hit, every shop [started copying the trend] with T-shirts.
upgrades.better: Once the show became a hit, every shop *jumped on the bandwagon* with T-shirts.

upgrades.plain: I refuse to [just follow everyone] and buy the new phone.
upgrades.better: I refuse to *jump on the bandwagon* and buy the new phone.

upgrades.plain: My uncle mocked electric cars for years, then [joined the trend] last month and now won't stop talking about it.
upgrades.better: My uncle mocked electric cars for years, then *jumped on the bandwagon* last month and now won't stop talking about it.

collocations.chunk: quick to jump on the bandwagon
refuse to jump on the bandwagon

nuance: Slightly mocking: it suggests people join for popularity or profit, not because they really care.
personal: When did you jump on the bandwagon with a trend you later regretted?
Who do you know who never jumps on the bandwagon, whatever is popular?
hook: Picture a parade wagon with a band on it; everyone leaps aboard only because the music is loud.

intents: never letting up, not even for a moment, with no break and no mercy
rain that pours for three days without a single pause
keeps pushing on and on, however tired everyone gets
ru_cue: не ослабевающий ни на минуту и не дающий передышки

upgrades.plain: The heat that August was [non-stop]; even the nights were hot.
upgrades.better: The heat that August was *relentless*; even the nights were hot.

upgrades.plain: My boss's [constant, never-ending] pressure before the launch had me crying in the toilets.
upgrades.better: My boss's *relentless* pressure before the launch had me crying in the toilets.

upgrades.plain: She trained at a [punishing, non-stop] pace and finally made the national team.
upgrades.better: She trained at a *relentless* pace and finally made the national team.

nuance: Relentless means it never eases off and can feel cruel; about a person, it praises (or fears) their unstoppable drive.
personal: When did you face relentless pressure, and how did you get through it?
Who do you know who is relentless once they set a goal?
hook: 'Re-LENT-less': the boss who has never lent anyone a single day off.

intents: extremely careful to get every tiny detail exactly right
someone who labels every jar, checks every figure twice and keeps every receipt
so precise and thorough that nothing is ever missed or left to chance
ru_cue: проверяющий каждую мелочь, чтобы все было идеально

upgrades.plain: My dad keeps [very careful, detailed] records of every bill.
upgrades.better: My dad keeps *meticulous* records of every bill.

upgrades.plain: Thanks to her [very careful] planning, the surprise party went perfectly.
upgrades.better: Thanks to her *meticulous* planning, the surprise party went perfectly.

upgrades.plain: He's [extremely careful about every detail] when he cooks, which drives me mad when I'm starving.
upgrades.better: He's *meticulous* when he cooks, which drives me mad when I'm starving.

nuance: Meticulous praises a person's careful way of working; for examining something closely to find faults, use scrutinise.
personal: What are you meticulous about, even if you're relaxed about everything else?
Who is the most meticulous person you know, and how does it show?
hook: 'METI-culous' sounds like 'метить' (to mark): he marks and labels every tiny detail.

intents: strike a deep personal chord because it feels true to your own experience
when someone describes exactly what you went through and you think 'yes, that's me'
connect with people and stay meaningful to them long after they hear it
ru_cue: задевать за живое, потому что совпадает с твоим собственным опытом

upgrades.plain: Her talk about moving to a new country really [meant a lot to me].
upgrades.better: Her talk about moving to a new country really *resonated* with me.

upgrades.plain: The advert didn't [connect with] young people at all.
upgrades.better: The advert didn't *resonate* with young people at all.

upgrades.plain: When my dad read that poem at grandma's funeral, it [touched everyone deeply].
upgrades.better: When my dad read that poem at grandma's funeral, it *resonated* with everyone.

ru_trap: Russian 'резонировать' sounds technical or bookish; English resonate is everyday for ideas and takes *with*: it resonated with me (not 'it resonated me').
nuance: Something resonates with you when it matches your own experience; when it simply brings a memory or feeling to mind, it evokes it.
personal: What film or book has resonated with you most in the last year?
Which friend's advice still resonates with you, and what was it?
hook: 'Re-SO-nate': like a guitar string that hums back when you sing its note, 'yes, me too'.

intents: bring a memory, feeling or picture back into someone's mind
when the smell of pine calls up a clear picture of childhood holidays in your mind
call up a particular mood or time without describing it directly
ru_cue: заставлять в голове ожить картину, чувство или воспоминание

upgrades.plain: The smell of the sea always [brings back] my childhood summers.
upgrades.better: The smell of the sea always *evokes* my childhood summers.

upgrades.plain: His paintings [make you feel] the heat and dust of the desert.
upgrades.better: His paintings *evoke* the heat and dust of the desert.

upgrades.plain: Hearing my late mum's favourite song in the shop [brought back] so many memories that I had to leave.
upgrades.better: Hearing my late mum's favourite song in the shop *evoked* so many memories that I had to leave.

ru_trap: Russian 'вызывать' covers both; use *cause* for problems or physical reactions (cause a headache) and *evoke* only for memories, images and feelings.
nuance: Evoke brings an image or feeling into the mind; it never means causing a physical effect, and the wistful feeling itself is being nostalgic.
personal: What smell evokes your childhood most strongly?
Which song evokes a particular person for you, and who is it?
hook: 'E-VOKE' sounds like 'вокал' (vocals): one note of an old song and the whole memory sings back.

intents: a gift you live with, like a talent or a home, that is at the same time a burden to you
when your talent for remembering everything feels like a gift from heaven one day and a punishment the next
something in your life you feel lucky to have and fed up with in equal measure
ru_cue: дар, который одновременно и радует, и мучает
plain: good and bad at the same time

upgrades.plain: Having a photographic memory is [a gift and a burden at once]: exams are easy, but I can't forget anything embarrassing.
upgrades.better: Having a photographic memory is *a blessing and a curse*: exams are easy, but I can't forget anything embarrassing.

upgrades.plain: Being the eldest child was [lucky and unlucky at the same time]; I had more freedom, but I always got the blame.
upgrades.better: Being the eldest child was *a blessing and a curse*; I had more freedom, but I always got the blame.

upgrades.plain: Living next to the beach is [heaven and hell at the same time] in summer.
upgrades.better: Living next to the beach is *a blessing and a curse* in summer.

collocations.chunk: both a blessing and a curse
a blessing and a curse rolled into one
collocations.frame: my big noisy family is ___ rolled into one

nuance: Usually about something personal you live with (a trait, a home, a gadget) that you both value and suffer from; a double-edged sword is a tool or move whose effects can turn against you, and a blessing in disguise is bad luck that turns out well.
personal: Which part of your personality is a blessing and a curse?
Whose job in your family is a blessing and a curse for them, and why?
hook: Picture a fairy granting your wish, and a little storm cloud following you everywhere ever since.
forms: both a blessing and a curse

intents: deeply and painfully want something you don't have, for a long time
when you've been stuck in a grey city for months and ache for the sea every single day
an aching wish for something far away that just won't go away
ru_cue: долго и мучительно мечтать о том, чего нет рядом

upgrades.plain: After six months in the city, I [really missed] the quiet of the countryside.
upgrades.better: After six months in the city, I *yearned* for the quiet of the countryside.

upgrades.plain: He has always [wanted so badly] to see the Northern Lights.
upgrades.better: He has always *yearned* to see the Northern Lights.

upgrades.plain: Stuck in hospital over New Year, she [desperately wanted] to be home with her kids.
upgrades.better: Stuck in hospital over New Year, she *yearned* to be home with her kids.

ru_trap: Russian 'тосковать по' tempts a direct object or 'yearn about'; English says yearn *for* something or yearn *to do* something.
nuance: Yearn is a deep, lasting, often sad wanting; it can reach towards the future or something never had, while nostalgic only looks back.
personal: What do you yearn for when you're away from home?
Which friend or relative yearns to live somewhere else, and where?
gesture: Reach one hand out slowly towards something far away and hold it there.
hook: Sounds like 'year': year after year you keep aching for the same thing.

intents: grow strong and healthy because the conditions are just right
when your herbs suddenly shoot up on a sunny windowsill
start doing really well and blossom once you're in the right place with the right support
ru_cue: бурно расти и развиваться, когда условия подходящие

upgrades.plain: Tomatoes [grow really well] in a warm, sunny spot.
upgrades.better: Tomatoes *flourish* in a warm, sunny spot.

upgrades.plain: My son was miserable at his old school, but he's [really doing well] at the new one.
upgrades.better: My son was miserable at his old school, but he's *flourishing* at the new one.

upgrades.plain: The little bakery has [grown and done really well] since it moved to the high street.
upgrades.better: The little bakery has *flourished* since it moved to the high street.

nuance: Flourish is growing well because conditions are good; doing well because of pressure or hardship is thriving on it.
personal: Where or when did you flourish most, and why?
Who do you know who flourished after a big change in their life?
hook: 'FLOUR-ish': add flour and yeast, and the dough rises big and healthy in a warm kitchen.

intents: slowly get smaller and smaller until hardly anything is left
when your savings shrink week by week while you're out of work
fade away bit by bit, like a crowd thinning out after the rain starts
ru_cue: постепенно таять, пока почти ничего не останется

upgrades.plain: Our food supplies [started running low] by the third day of the hike.
upgrades.better: Our food supplies began to *dwindle* by the third day of the hike.

upgrades.plain: The crowd [slowly got smaller] once it started raining.
upgrades.better: The crowd *dwindled* once it started raining.

upgrades.plain: Only six people came to my book club last week; numbers have [been shrinking] all year and I'm scared it will close.
upgrades.better: Only six people came to my book club last week; numbers have been *dwindling* all year and I'm scared it will close.

nuance: Dwindle is a gradual, natural shrinking towards almost nothing; when someone limits something on purpose, they curb it.
personal: What have you watched dwindle over the years: a hobby, your savings, your free time?
Which relative's circle of friends has dwindled over the years, and why?
gesture: Start with your hands wide apart and slowly bring them together until they almost touch.
hook: 'Dwindle' sounds like 'два-один-ноль' (two-one-zero): the count drops until nothing is left.
